readings.title: A Song for the Sabbath Day
readings.subtitle: It is Good to Give Thanks
readings.text: [Psalm 92:1] It is good to give thanks to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, And to sing praises to <dn>Your</dn> Name, O Most High; [2] To declare <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment in the morning, And <dn>Your</dn> trustworthiness each night, [3] On ten strings, and on the harp, To the sounding chords of the lyre. [4] For <dn>You</dn> have made <dn>me</dn> rejoice with <dn>Your</dn> work, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>I</dn> shout for joy at the works of <dn>Your</dn> hands.

readings.title: The Greatness of YeHoVaH's Works
readings.subtitle: The Fool Does Not Understand
readings.text: [Psalm 92:5] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, how great are <dn>Your</dn> works! <dn>Your</dn> thoughts are very deep! [6] A senseless man does not know, And a fool does not understand this. [7] When the wrong spring up like grass, And all the workers of wickedness blossom, It is for them to be destroyed forever. [8] But <dn>You</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, are on high forever. [9] For look, <dn>Your</dn> enemies, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, For look, <dn>Your</dn> enemies do perish; All the workers of wickedness are scattered.

readings.title: The Flourishing of the Righteous
readings.subtitle: Planted in the House of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Psalm 92:10] But <dn>You</dn> lift up <dn>my</dn> horn like a wild ox; <dn>I</dn> have been anointed with fresh oil. [11] And <dn>my</dn> eye looks upon <dn>my</dn> enemies; <dn>My</dn> ears hear the evil-doers Who rise up against <dn>me</dn>. [12] The righteous one flourishes like a palm tree, <dn>He</dn> grows like a cedar in Leḇanon. [13] Those who are planted in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> Flourish in the courts of our <dn>Elohim</dn>. [14] They still bear fruit in old age; They are fresh and green, [15] To declare that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is straight, <dn>My</dn> rock, and in <dn>Him</dn> is no unrighteousness.

readings.title: The Eternal Reign of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: Mightier Than the Mighty Breakers of the Sea
readings.text: [Psalm 93:1] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall reign, <dn>He</dn> shall put on excellency; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall put on strength; <dn>He</dn> shall gird <dn>Himself</dn>. Indeed, the world is established, immovable. [2] <dn>Your</dn> throne is established from of old; <dn>You</dn> are from everlasting. [3] Rivers shall lift up, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Rivers shall lift up their voice; Rivers lift up their breakers. [4] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on high is mightier Than the noise of many waters, The mighty breakers of the sea. [5] <dn>Your</dn> witnesses have been very trustworthy. Set-apartness befits <dn>Your</dn> house, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, forever.

readings.title: A Plea for Divine Vengeance
readings.subtitle: How Long, O YeHoVaH?
readings.text: [Psalm 94:1] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>Ěl</dn> of vengeance; O <dn>Ěl</dn> of vengeance, shine forth! [2] Raise <dn>Yourself</dn> up, O Judge of the earth; Render punishment to the proud. [3] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, how long are the wrong, How long are the wrong going to exult? [4] They pour forth words, They speak arrogantly; All the workers of wickedness boast in themselves. [5] They crush <dn>Your</dn> people, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, And they afflict <dn>Your</dn> inheritance. [6] They kill the widow and the stranger, And murder the fatherless. [7] Yet they say, “<dn>Yah</dn> does not see, And the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya‛aqoḇ pays no heed.”

readings.title: The Folly of the Wicked and the Blessing of Discipline
readings.subtitle: He Who Planted the Ear, Does He Not Hear?
readings.text: [Psalm 94:8] Take heed, you senseless among the people; And you fools, when would you become wise? [9] <dn>He</dn> who planted the ear, does <dn>He</dn> not hear? <dn>He</dn> who formed the eye, does <dn>He</dn> not see? [10] <dn>He</dn> who disciplines the nations, Does <dn>He</dn> not reprove – The One teaching man knowledge? [11] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> knows the thoughts of man, That they are but a breath. [12] Blessed is the man <dn>You</dn> discipline, O <dn>Yah</dn>, And instruct out of <dn>Your</dn> Torah, [13] To give him rest from the days of evil, Until the pit is dug for the wrong. [14] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does not leave <dn>His</dn> people, Nor does <dn>He</dn> forsake <dn>His</dn> inheritance. [15] For right-ruling returns man to righteousness, And all the upright in heart follow it.

readings.title: YeHoVaH, My Help and My Defense
readings.subtitle: The Rock of My Refuge
readings.text: [Psalm 94:16] Who would rise up for <dn>me</dn> against evil-doers? Who would stand up for <dn>me</dn> against workers of wickedness? [17] If <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had not been <dn>my</dn> help, <dn>My</dn> being would soon have settled in silence. [18] When <dn>I</dn> said, “<dn>My</dn> foot has slipped,” <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, supported <dn>me</dn>. [19] When anxiety was great within <dn>me</dn>, <dn>Your</dn> comforts delighted <dn>my</dn> being. [20] Would a throne of destruction, Which devises trouble by law, Be joined with <dn>You</dn>? [21] They band together against the life of the righteous, And declare innocent blood wrong. [22] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is <dn>my</dn> defence, And <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> the rock of <dn>my</dn> refuge, [23] And brings back on them their own wickedness, And cuts them off in their own wrongdoing; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> does cut them off.

readings.title: A Call to Joyful Worship
readings.subtitle: Let Us Raise a Shout to the Rock of Our Deliverance
readings.text: [Psalm 95:1] Come, let us sing to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! Let us raise a shout to the Rock of our deliverance. [2] Let us come before <dn>His</dn> face with thanksgiving; Let us raise a shout to <dn>Him</dn> in song. [3] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is a great <dn>Ěl</dn>, And a great Sovereign above all mighty ones. [4] In whose hand are the depths of the earth; The mountain peaks are <dn>His</dn> also. [5] <dn>His</dn> is the sea, for <dn>He</dn> made it; And <dn>His</dn> hands formed the dry land. [6] Come, let us bow down and bend low, Let us kneel before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our Maker. [7] For <dn>He</dn> is our <dn>Elohim</dn>, And we are the people of <dn>His</dn> pasture, And the sheep of <dn>His</dn> hand. Today, if you would hear <dn>His</dn> voice:

readings.title: A Warning Against a Hardened Heart
readings.subtitle: As in the Day of Massah in the Wilderness
readings.text: [Psalm 95:8] <dq>“Do not harden your hearts as in Meriḇah, And as in the day of Massah in the wilderness,</dq> [9] <dq>“When your fathers tried <dn>Me</dn>, Have proved <dn>Me</dn>, though they saw <dn>My</dn> work.</dq> [10] <dq>“For forty years <dn>I</dn> was grieved with that generation, And said, ‘They are a people who go astray in their hearts, And they do not know <dn>My</dn> ways.’</dq> [11] <dq>“As <dn>I</dn> swore in <dn>My</dn> wrath, ‘If they enter into <dn>My</dn> rest...’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Sing a New Song to YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: Declare His Esteem Among the Nations
readings.text: [Psalm 96:1] Sing to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> a new song, Sing to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, all the earth! [2] Sing to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, bless <dn>His</dn> Name, Proclaim <dn>His</dn> deliverance from day to day. [3] Declare <dn>His</dn> esteem among the nations, <dn>His</dn> wonders among all peoples. [4] For great is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and greatly to be praised, <dn>He</dn> is to be feared above all mighty ones. [5] For all the mighty ones of the peoples are matters of naught, But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made the heavens. [6] Excellency and splendour are before <dn>Him</dn>, Strength and comeliness are in <dn>His</dn> set-apart place.

readings.title: Ascribe Glory to the Coming King
readings.subtitle: He Shall Come to Judge the Earth
readings.text: [Psalm 96:7] Ascribe to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, O clans of the peoples, Ascribe to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> esteem and strength. [8] Ascribe to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> the esteem of <dn>His</dn> Name; Bring an offering, and come into <dn>His</dn> courts. [9] Bow yourselves to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, In the splendour of set-apartness! Tremble before <dn>Him</dn>, all the earth. [10] Say among nations, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall reign. The world also is established, immovable. <dn>He</dn> judges the peoples in straightness.” [11] Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad; Let the sea roar, and all that fills it; [12] Let the field exult, and all that is in it. Let all the trees of the forest then shout for joy, [13] At the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. For <dn>He</dn> shall come, For <dn>He</dn> shall come to judge the earth. <dn>He</dn> judges the world in righteousness, And the peoples with <dn>His</dn> truth.

readings.title: The Majestic Reign of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: The Mountains Shall Melt Like Wax
readings.text: [Psalm 97:1] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall reign. The earth rejoices. Many isles are glad! [2] Clouds and darkness all around <dn>Him</dn>, Righteousness and right-ruling are the foundation of <dn>His</dn> throne. [3] Fire goes before <dn>Him</dn>, And burns up <dn>His</dn> adversaries round about. [4] <dn>His</dn> lightnings shall light the world, The earth shall see and tremble. [5] The mountains shall melt like wax before the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Before the face of the Master of all the earth. [6] The heavens shall declare <dn>His</dn> righteousness, And all the peoples shall see <dn>His</dn> esteem.

readings.title: The Response to His Reign
readings.subtitle: Rejoice in YeHoVaH, You Righteous
readings.text: [Psalm 97:7] All are put to shame who serve carved images, Those boasting of matters of naught. Bow yourselves to <dn>Him</dn>, all you mighty ones. [8] Tsiyon shall hear and be glad, And the daughters of Yehuḏah rejoice Because of <dn>Your</dn> right-rulings, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [9] For <dn>You</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, are the Most High over all the earth, <dn>You</dn> shall be greatly exalted, over all mighty ones. [10] You who love <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, hate evil! <dn>He</dn> guards the lives of <dn>His</dn> lovingly-committed ones, <dn>He</dn> delivers them out of the hand of the wrong. [11] Light is sown for the righteous, And gladness for the upright in heart. [12] Rejoice in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, you righteous, And give thanks at the remembrance of <dn>His</dn> Set-apartness.
